# GREEN ZONE — Xbox Fan Arcade

Since "Xbox" was the whole brief, I built an original, unofficial Xbox-inspired arcade survival game. No Microsoft assets or branding are used — just the green-and-black energy, an original sphere-style mark, and a "Not affiliated with Microsoft" disclaimer.

## Play it

```bash
cd /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround
python3 -m http.server 3002
```

Open http://localhost:3002. It's already running in tmux session `gz`.

## What it is

A twin-stick arena survival game on a 2D canvas with synthesized WebAudio — no dependencies, no build step:

- **Auto-fire** at the nearest target; you focus on movement.
- **Rechargeable shields** instead of one-hit deaths, plus a **dash** with invincibility frames.
- **Combo multiplier** that rewards aggressive, uninterrupted play.
- **Pickups**, escalating waves, and a **Sentinel boss every 5th wave** with radial/aimed patterns and adds.
- Local best score, rank labels, pause/game-over flows.

## Controls

| Action | Keyboard / Mouse | Gamepad | Touch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Move | WASD / arrows | Left stick | Left thumbstick |
| Aim | Mouse | Right stick | Right thumbstick |
| Dash | Space / right-click | A / RT | Center DASH button |
| Pause | Esc | Start | HUD pause button |
| Mute | M | — | Audio toggle |

## Files

- `index.html`, `styles.css` — markup, screens, HUD, responsive layout
- `js/game.js` — engine, waves, boss, collisions, rendering
- `js/input.js` — unified keyboard/mouse/gamepad/touch input
- `js/audio.js` — WebAudio SFX and ambient pad
- `js/main.js` — boot, menus, HUD diffing, game loop
- `README.md` — GREEN ZONE section with play instructions and disclaimer
- `screenshots/` — verified desktop, mobile, landscape, boss, and menu captures (gitignored)

## Verification

Tested in Chromium at 1440×900, 844×390, 390×844, and 320×568. Keyboard, mouse, touch dual-stick, and a stubbed gamepad all drive the game; pause/resume, retry, quit-to-menu, mute, and auto-pause on tab blur work. All assets return 200 and the console is clean. In this headless software-rendered environment the full-screen canvas caps around 7–10 fps; profiling shows game logic and render commands cost under 1 ms per frame, so that ceiling is the Xvfb/SwiftShader rasterizer, not the game.
